OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIAMOND ENERGY PARTNERS LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 8/11/2022
Violation Code: OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
Violation ID: 964695
Permit API: 085-24071
Unconventional: No
County: Mercer
Municipality: Delaware Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/11/2022
Comments: Arrived at location on 8/11/2022 to met with Operator representatives work crew (Diamond Energy), late morning with cool, cloudy weather conditions, and 72 degrees. Activities from yesterday (8/10/22) include the following: Minor leak at lower casing collar union repaired. Operator addressed/repaired this union leak yesterday (8/10/22) by entering the well, setting down tubing, lower wellhead, secure well and make repair to casing collar union at wellhead. The wellhead, unions, valves, meter, and tubulars have all been replaced and plumbed (photos #1 and #2). All old parts and materials disposed of due to fire damage. Production copper fittings, lines, and logix system to be installed tomorrow (8/12/22). The well was being vented/produced to sales line and recorded on a newly installed 31-day production chart while repairing (photo #3). Utilizing the 100 bbl steel tank at the ground production facility as additional vent for spill prevention. The tank vent is open to atmosphere (photo #4). The Mechanical integrity of well and repairs checked this morning (8/11/22) with pressure gauge. The well is holding ~1,100 psi on production tubing and is temporarily shut in at present. Routine and complete inspection in response to incident of well catching fire after a lightning strike that was witnessed by the property land owner during a thunderstorm on August 5, 2022 at approximately 2042 hours. The address for the property is 18 Wasser Road, Greenville, PA 16125. The well is located in Delaware Township, Mercer County, PA. The well is operated, since 2020 by Diamond Energy Partners with issued permit number 085-24071 on 4/13/2006, spud date was on 8/31/2007, drilled to total depth of 5,290 feet, Site ID# 669360, and is a conventional vertical gas well. Wellhead is located in livestock pasture/field and ~550' WNW of surface/ground production equipment. The surface/ground production equipment, one 100 bbl steel, and one 50 bbl poly tank(s) are contained by earthen dike (photos #4). Operator has temporarily written well details as well posting on 100 bbl steel tank to suffice for the interim until a permanent posting is affixed (photo #4). Fair to occasionally moderate corrosion on ground production unit equipment and steel tanks. Continued Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). The mechanical integrity assessment (MIA) report and submitted by Operator (Diamond) for 2021 for this well states 800 psig. The last reported, commercial production was in 2016 of 1,081 MCF recorded over 84 days by former Operator, Bobcat Well and Pipeline. The 2021 annual production report (APR) submitted by present Operator (Diamond) indicates that this well was not in production during the 2021 production year. Additionally, this well was noted as having 0 production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns and noted as Well Temporarily Not Producing under the non production comments columns of the 2021 production report. There is mention of domestic house gas under additional comments column on 2017 and 2018 APRs, but not mentioned in prior or post years. In talking with the property land owner (8/8/22), domestic house gas has been provided uninterruptedly to residence since the initial drilling of the well back in 2007. Conversation with the Operator (Diamond) also concurs domestic house gas supply to landowner. Albeit no commercial production to sales reported by Operator, stating 0 production under the gas and/or oil quantity columns, the well is active and providing domestic house gas continuously and will be restored once repairs to wellhead are completed. The Department is requesting the Operator (Diamond) provide a copy of the Preparedness Prevention and Contingency Plan (PPC) document for this well and well site facility.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/01/2024 to RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC in South Franklin Township, Washington county. SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP.  Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: RANGE RESOURCES APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/01/2024
Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8206533
Permit API: 125-29107
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: South Franklin Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 11/01/2024
Comments: On 11/01/2024 a Complaint Inspection was conducted at the Folly Hollow Farm Unit OG Well Pad in response to a suspected release reported by multiple landowners. PA DEP Oil and Gas Inspector Supervisor Scott Sabocheck and Range Resources Representatives, Barry Bugbee and Nick Reda were on site at the time of inspection.Conductivity probe calibrated on 11/01/2024.The following was observed during the inspection:-An area of staining was observed beneath a flare stack located off secondary containment. Mr. Bugbee indicated that fluid was released, in a mist, from the flare stack yesterday(10/31/24) between 8:30 and 9:00 am, that the quantity released was approximately 2 gallons, and that the impacted material, except for the portion beneath the flare stack, was removed immediately after the release. The area of removed material and stained material combined appeared to be approximately 10 ft long by 10 ft wide in an irregular shape. The Department requests clarification on how the quantity released was determined (Photo 1).-Field conductivity screening was conducted within the area of stained material around and beneath the flare stack. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 3.74 and 11.01 ms/cm (Photos 2-4).-Fluid was actively being released onto secondary containment during the plug removal from the well associated with the American Petroleum Institute (API) number 125-29107. Range Resources representative stated that the fluid released was fresh water (Photos 5-6).-Field conductivity screening was conducted within the area of fluid located in secondary containment. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 5.41 ms/cm and Over Range (OR), which equates to greater than 20 ms/cm (Photos 7-9).-During the inspection, the flare stack was broken down and removed and the impacted material was excavated. The pad aggregate was removed to a depth of approximately 1-3 inches. The final area of removed material measured approximately 10 ft long by 10 ft wide (Photos 10-11).-Post-remediation field conductivity screening was conducted. Field conductivity readings were observed to be between 0.8 and 35.5 s/cm (Photos 12-15). Determination:Because the impacted material was removed and post-remediation screening values were below standard, violations of 78.57(a), 78a54, and SWMA 301 are being issued and immediately corrected.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/12/2026
Violation Code: OGA3216(B) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PLAN - Failure to follow E&S control plan during and after earthmoving or soil disturbing activities.
Violation ID: 8274769
Permit API: 051-21886
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: German Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/12/2026
Comments: On May 12, 2026, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 4179368.A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, Diversified shall restore the site within 9 months of Well plugging in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act, 58 Pa. C.S. 3216. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 2/23/2026, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 11/23/2026 in accordance with current regulations.During today's inspection, the following was observed:- E and S plans on site have not been updated as stated in the NOV Response (IR 4166188). The plans appear to be unchanged and do not include wetland delineations in any of the drawings or added wetland seed mix(es) to Detail 06.- CFS near the access road entrance is not properly installed at this time (Photo 5).- Gravel from the RCE remains on site. The Department recommends the operator remove all gravel that is not pre-existing from the site.- A berm appears to have been constructed (Photo 7). The Department requests information regarding the purpose of the berm and if it is to remain post-restoration.- The site appears to have been seeded and mulched, with vegetation growing in some areas at this time.- What appears to be third party disturbance in the form of a two track trail is observed from the access road through site, and exiting over CFS (Photos 7-8, 11, 13, 15, 23).- CFS surrounding the site is improperly installed (Photos 11, 12, 21) including portions that have been repaired multiple times causing the sock to flatten. The Department recommends the operator replace the repaired portions of CFS.- CFS where the surface water exits the site appears to be failing, showing signs of overtopping and undercutting. The Department recommends the operator replace the current CFS and properly maintain CFS on site until restoration is achieved.- The absorbent pads that were left on site by the operator appear to remain on site at this time. The Department recommends the operator remove the absorbent pads from the site.Violations remain outstanding at this time.

Comments: On 4/22/2026, a follow-up inspection to IR 4164849 was conducted, where violations were issued in response to reported sloughing at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. The sloughing was reportedly discovered by the operator on 3/20/2026, on the cutslope above the access road.An Individual Erosion and Sedimentation permit (ESP) was issued by the Department for this site on 1/26/2024 and expires on 1/25/2029.The following was observed during the inspection:The sloughing remains on the cutslope above the access road, as reported by the operator on 3/20/2026 (photos 19-21). This area appears to be unchanged since the time of 4164849 and does not appear to immediately threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. No pipeline markers and/or gas well equipment were observed below the slough. Temporary stabilization is applied to the slough. Repairs are reportedly expected to begin once the ground dries adequately to allow for machine operation.The former slope repair area north of the well pad has nearly established 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage (photos 12 and 13). However, temporary stabilization was observed on a small portion of the other former slope repair area south of the well pad (photos 14 and 15). The Department requests clarification from the operator regarding what occurred in this location and why temporary stabilization was applied. Please provide this clarification electronically to the Department no later than 5/01/2026. Violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator's response. The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observable concerns relating to accelerated erosion and sedimentation (photos 1 and 22). Post-Construction Stormwater Management Best Management Practices (PCSM BMP) appear to be constructed in the locations shown on the approved ESP plan drawings (photos 16-18).The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 23). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Erosion and Sedimentation (E and S) inspection log, and ESP approval letter are on site (photos 2-6). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Seven gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 11). Well 6H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 24). The well and operator's information are displayed and visible on this well tag, as required by OGA 3211(g) and OGA 3211(h).The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection (photo 7). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units on site are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 9 and 10). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4164849 shall remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 955511
Permit API: 035-21325
Unconventional: Yes

Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/12/2022
Comments: On May 12, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow up inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Well Pad. This is follow up inspection to a spill of production fluid of an estimated 1,600 barrels, when a hose broke on a frac tank. The production fluid overflowed the containment of the frac tanks and spilled on to the pad surface and flowed off of the well pad. The area where the water was seeping out near the northwest stormwater vault observed on March 3, 2022 was not flowing. The small berm that was built to collect the seep was was dry and any water that is collected in that area is being vacuumed out. Upon arrival at the well pad, STL Resources was vacuuming water out of the northwest stormwater vault. The conductivity of the water that could not be vacuumed out was 2,500 uS/cm. About 18 inches of water was in the southwest stormwater vault. The water was not high enough in this vault to be measured for conductivity due to not being able to reach the water levels with the field water quality meter. STL Resources has back filled and rebuilt the excavated southwest and northwest infiltration berms that were impacted by the spill. DEP screened the water that had pooled up behind the northwest infiltration for conductivity and that resulted in 187 uS/cm. The conductivity of the small amount of water that pooled up behind the southwest infiltration berm was 40 uS/cm. The DEP screened the five seeps and four stream sampling sites for conductivity with a field water quality meter. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 1 (4) had conductivity of 21.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 2 (3) had conductivity of 22.1 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 3 (2) had a conductivity of 24.4 uS/cm. UNT to Rattlesnake Run site 4 (1) had a conductivity of 23.1 uS/cm. Seep 1 had a conductivity of 188 uS/cm. Seep 1a had a conductivity of 196.2 uS/cm. Seep 2 had a conductivity of 59.9 uS/cm. Seep 3 had a conductivity of 44.8 uS/cm. Seep 4 had a conductivity of 133.4 uS/cm. Seep 5 had a conductivity of 25.2 uS/cm. Stream site names have been reorganized by STL Resources consults. The numbers in parentheses at the end of the site names are the original numbers and the number outside the parentheses are the current numbers. During the inspection, STL Resources consultants were collecting soil samples from the well pad in a grid like pattern to delineate the area of the production fluid spill. Comments: On 4/22/2026, a follow-up inspection to IR 4164849 was conducted, where violations were issued in response to reported sloughing at the Schwotzer Arthur well site in Blaine Township, Washington County. This area appears to be unchanged since the time of 4164849 and does not appear to immediately threaten the Waters of the Commonwealth. No pipeline markers and/or gas well equipment were observed below the slough. Temporary stabilization is applied to the slough. Repairs are reportedly expected to begin once the ground dries adequately to allow for machine operation.The former slope repair area north of the well pad has nearly established 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth coverage (photos 12 and 13). However, temporary stabilization was observed on a small portion of the other former slope repair area south of the well pad (photos 14 and 15). The Department requests clarification from the operator regarding what occurred in this location and why temporary stabilization was applied. Please provide this clarification electronically to the Department no later than 5/01/2026. Violations may be forthcoming pending receipt and review of operator's response. The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Seven gas wells are on site that appear to be equipped for production (photo 11). Well 6H is equipped with a well tag with no observable evidence of a fluid leak to the ground around it (photo 24). The GPU/Vertical Separator Units on site are equipped with interconnected secondary containment drip pans (photos 9 and 10). This form of GPU secondary containment was approved by the Department for use on 6/21/2022.Based on observations from this inspection, violations issued in IR 4164849 shall remain outstanding.

Comments: This inspection was performed following a report of a possible spill/breached containment at the Beechwood Pad A site. (CTS #348135). The site was inspected for evidence of lack of secondary containment around equipment and/or spills. The production fluid tank site was inspected. This site contains three 400 barrel tanks. The area behind (on the north side) of the tank site was checked and there was some liquid beneath the ice in the ditch. The fluids were contained in their separate containments. The separator was set in containment that had blocks set up for holding tanks that have been removed. The containment itself was dry and it was noted that there were several holes in the liner, which would allow any spilled fluid to leak out of containment. The area around the wellheads is clean and no evidence of spills was noted. The site ID sign is on site with well and pad information.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/09/2022
Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's VanBlarcom R 03-113 well site located in Columbia Township, Bradford County on 2/9/2022 at 1025 hours. The weather was 34 degrees with partly cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported by the operator. Complaint ID #362029 is tied to the release within CTS. On 2/6/2022 at approximately 1500 hours a release of approximately 15 gallons of produced water and 3 gallons of glycol were released to the pad surface. A leaking produced water flow-line released the produced water directly beneath where the leak occurred. Insulation on the flow-line contained the released to the small area beneath the line. The release on the produced water flow-line caused a crack on a pex pipe near the GPU unit which released the glycol to the pad surface. Both areas were observed today having snow, ice and slush removed from the pad surface. It appears as though the snow absorbed the majority of the releases. I collected some snow beneath the produced water flow-line and allowed it to melt. The melted snow was field measured at ~155us/cm. The releases are both cleaned up to visible (photos #5 & 6). Barrels containing the impacted material were observed in the GPU secondary containment (photo #4). I spoke with Mark Watson (Repsol) over the phone while I was onsite. He explained that a leaking pipe on the produced water flow-line caused fluid to kick back, cracking a pex pipe on the GPU. The leaking produced water flow-line was reported to release ~15 gallons of produced water to the pad surface. The cracked pex pipe was reported to release ~3 gallons of glycol to the pad surface. properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-06-03 to Catalyst Energy Inc in Hamilton Twp, McKean county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Catalyst Energy Inc
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-06-03
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 886011
Permit API: 083-55763
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Hamilton Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-06-03
Comments: This well is a producing combination well with an electric powered motor attached. The well was being operated at the time of this inspection. The stuffing box gasket failed, and at the time of visit, the well was pumping oil and brine out to the ground. The fluid plus runoff from recent rains allowed the oil to flow down the road approximately 150 feet, entering a puddle near a culvert that carried an UNT Chappel Fork. The operator was contacted to get cleanup efforts underway. The well was shut off and pads were placed down to collect as much oil from the track as possible. No oil was apparent in the UNT. Rain stopped and there was a decrease in the flow of oil down the track. The pumper for this lease showed up and was able to leave and get a vacuum truck to come collect the water/oil in the puddle. Marking tape was placed so that public vehicles would not drive through the oil. It is estimated that 15-20 gallons of fluid, including 3-5 gallons of oil were released from the well due to the stuffing box failure. Most pooled in a low spot next to the wellhead. Some ran down the access road, again pooling in a puddle of water that was previously mentioned. The brine mostly stayed in place in the soil or vegetation. A puddle within 10 feet of the wellhead showed over 20 mS/cm conductivity, while checking further toward the extent of the spill showed much lower numbers. The final puddle registered under 0.1 mS/cm. The operator had the vac truck on the way and after later discussions, it was decided that they would need to excavate the area around the wellhead to remove impacted soil. Further follow up will be done on this site as possible.

Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of Blackhill Energy's Ashby 1H (A) well site located Athens Township, Bradford County on 4/5/2023 at 1030 hours. The weather was 63 degrees with partly cloudy skies. Complaint tracking system (CTS) ID #371126 is tied to this release within CTS.On 4/4/2023 at ~1430 hours, a release of approximately 7 gallons of produced water occurred at the Ashby pad after a hose wasn't emptied prior to disconnecting from the offload valve of the produced water tank. The trucking company returned to the site and recovered the produced water on the surface but didn't fully recover all the impacted pad material. When I arrived onsite, pad material in the impacted area (photos #2 and 3) was field measured for electrical conductivity and returned readings of >4.00mS/cm. All standing water that I field measured for electrical conductivity on the pad surface returned readings ranging 400 to 700us/cm. Code 78a.56(a), 35 P.S. 6018.301, and 35 P.S. 691.402(b) are cited against API #015-21997. These violations will be cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED based on Blackhill Energy's timely remedial response.I departed the site at 1130 hours.

Violation ID: 931500
Permit API: 003-22145
Unconventional: No
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Harmar Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/24/2021
Comments: Inspection in response to a discharge of gas and crude oil from this well reported to the Department at 0250. The County HazMat Team and Department ERT were called to the incident and reported the incident as venting of crude oil and gas from a pressure relief valve on top of a tank. During the response, it was reported that the pump jack eventually stopped operating and the discharge of crude oil tapered off and essentially stopped. The valve continued to vent natural gas. The County HazMat Team strung caution tape around the well site, laid down pig matting where crude oil had sprayed and absorbent booms around the puddles of crude oil (Photos 1-8). Accompanying me during inspection is OGI Jon Shub (DEP) and Josh Boarts, the well tender for the operator. Boarts began clean up efforts by filling buckets with the oil that surrounded the well head and dumping it into the brine tank on site (Photo 9). Boarts then laid down pig matting around all affected areas and then absorb-it on the areas around the pump jack and well head (Photos 20-23). The spill was generally contained within the area of which the yellow tape is surrounding the site. The area around the well is flat aside from the depression around the pump jack that allowed the crude oil to pool around it. The closest Water of the Commonwealth is Deer Creek which is approximately 300 feet East of the well, but does not appear to be in danger of contamination due to the flat parking lot in which the well sits. According to the owner of the property, who has a video feed of the well, the discharge began at approximately 22:04 on 9/23. Oil had discharged up until the early morning when the HazMat team was on site. Josh Boarts estimated the spill to be around half a barrel while on site. The exact cause of why the pressure valve was released is unknown to the operator at this time, but the well tender Josh Boarts did say the valve is supposed to release at 250 lbs of pressure. Boarts was provided with the Department spill policy and program clarification memo. Boarts plans to gather visibly impacted material into large barrels before properly removing them off site.

Comments: On 02/14/2024, a routine complete inspection was conducted at the Hixenbaugh 1-P060 well. I notified Joel Greco of KPI ("operator"), regarding my findings on 02/14/2024. It was noted that there was rig work recently conducted onsite and that there were some things to address/clean up. The following was observed during the inspection:Well tags displaying the well and operators information were noted on site (Photos 1, 2).A methanol drum was noted on site. Although not required, I recommended placing containers within secondary containment to avoid substances from reaching the ground. Mr. Greco noted that the drum was empty and used for tubing that was experiencing freezing/thawing issues. I recommend that any unnecessary material is removed from the site and disposed of properly (Photos 3-5). In a 06/16/2017 compliance evaluation inspection (Inspection Report 2614040), a methanol drum was noted onsite without secondary containment and a violation of 91.34(a) was issued on 09/20/2016 (Inspection Report 2532594, Enforcement 348270).There was a spot of grease-like material on the ground near the tubing. properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Ard Opr Llc

Violation Code: SWMA 301 - MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person operated a residual waste processing or disposal facility without obtaining a permit for such facility from DEP. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 866621
Permit API: 035-21253
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clinton
Municipality: Grugan Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-10-30
Comments: On October 30, 2019 , DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a spill investigation (CTS # 346141) at Alta Operating LLC. COP Tract 285 Pad G. The spill was reported at 0935 that a plug in the dump line of one of the GPUs was not replaced after maintenance on the line was completed. This caused a spill of about 1.9 bbls into the secondary containment and the pad surface. The DEP met with Alta staff Rick Hall and Mark Barbier, they estimated that about a 1 bbl was spilled outside of containment. During the investigation, there was a vacuum tank onsite dewatering the secondary containment of the GPUs. There is a ground wire in the area of the spill, so they were awaiting staff to locate the wire before excavation of the impacted soil could begin. The area of impact is approximately 10'x60'. Water in the secondary containment was screened for conductivity and returned a reading of 1070 uS/cm. A puddle of water in the impacted area was screened and returned a conductivity reading of 5,500 uS/cm. One 25 yard rollback dumpster was onsite to dispose of the impacted soil. The release of production fluid outside of secondary containment is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Section 301 of the Solid Waste Management Act and §78a.54. Due to the volume of the production fluid spilled outside of containment, characterization of the extent of the pollution in accordance of §78a.66(c). The DEP recommends proceeding in accordance with Act 2 remediation.

Inspection Date: 9/19/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that on 9/18/23 a leak was discovered in a GPU on Pad A which led to the release of an unknown quantity of produced fluid to the pad surface. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad A. He showed me where the produced fluid leak occurred inside of GPU #3. He also showed me where the fluid overflowed the interior containment of the GPU and flowed outside of the GPU and onto the pad surface to the southwest of the GPU. A Waste Management crew was excavating the impacted area of the pad during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that the fluid appears to have traveled a couple of inches into the pad surface and then moved toward the southwest pad edge under the surface. A sump present in the stormwater channel along the southwest side of the pad had fluid in it with an electrical conductivity (EC) of 700 uS/cm. Mr. Subra stated that the initial EC reading taken in this sump was approximately 700 uS/cm and later it increased to approximately 1700 uS/cm. A smaller puddle of fluid approximately 25 feet to the north in the channel had an EC of 760 uS/cm during this inspection. No other fluid was observed in the channel or on the pad surface. The Department recommends vacuuming out the fluid in the southwest stormwater channel.Mr. Subra said that they plan to pursue Act 2 remediation due to the unknown volume of the release. Environmental consultant Penn E and R was present during this inspection. Mr. Subra said that Penn E and R were performing electrical conductivity screening and would take samples for the Act 2 remediation. Violations noted against permit 081-21855 for the produced fluid release to the surface of Pad A.Violations remain outstanding for the produced fluid release to Pad B from 12/19/22.
